extracted.intended_audience: education researchers applying to the Spencer Foundation for research funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for applicants preparing Letters of Intent and full proposals to the Spencer Foundation (Small, Large, Vision, Racial Equity, and Lyle Spencer awards). Focuses on what reviewers evaluate and program fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous, intellectually ambitious and technically sound research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation's goal is to support rigorous, intellectually ambitious and technically sound research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate strong methodological rigor and intellectual ambition rather than incremental work; technical soundness across chosen methods is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant to the most pressing questions and compelling opportunities in education
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should be relevant to the most pressing questions and compelling opportunities in education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for centrality and topical importance to the field of education — work that addresses timely or consequential problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative and open-minded scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation seeks creative and open-minded scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel approaches, openness to multiple perspectives, and intellectual creativity are valued in framing and conducting projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should aim for deep inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects are expected to engage substantively with their topic, not superficial treatments; depth of theoretical and empirical engagement is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust questions related to education
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should pose robust questions related to education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, well-formulated research questions that drive the study and are central to educational concerns are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship that develops new foundational knowledge with potential lasting impact on policy-making, practice, or educational discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation prioritizes scholarship that develops new foundational knowledge with potential lasting impact on policy-making, practice, or educational discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate potential longer-term impacts on policy, practice, or public discourse and how findings could influence these areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of the Project
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate centrality of education in the research, importance of the topic to its field, quality of the research question(s), and direction of inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the project matters for education and its field; demonstrate that the questions are important, timely, and promise meaningful contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection to Research and Theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate adequacy of the description of how other researchers have treated the same topic, how well the proposal responds to prior work and theory, and the theoretical framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate the study in existing literature, clearly articulate theoretical framing, and show how the project builds on or challenges prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate overall quality, sophistication, and appropriateness of the research design, and its alignment with the research question(s) and conceptual framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a design that is methodologically appropriate and aligned to the questions and theory; justify chosen methods, sampling, analytic strategies, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate adequacy of the budget, adequacy of the timeline, and strength of proposal within their funding tier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a realistic, well-justified budget and timeline that match project scope and the chosen funding program (e.g., small vs large grants); demonstrate fiscal responsibility and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Team
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers comment on the potential of the investigator(s) to complete the study as described and the potential to share the results or other findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate investigator expertise, complementary team skills, and capacity to carry out the project and disseminate findings; include plans for collaboration and management if multi-person team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate proposed plans for sharing the results, which may include traditional submissions to conferences or publications, other efforts aimed at influencing research, policy, practice, or public discourse, stakeholder engagement, and open access and data sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete dissemination strategies targeting academic and non-academic audiences, stakeholder engagement approaches, and commitments to open access or data sharing where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Research Grants eligibility/fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Small Research Grants ($50K) are for exploratory or pilot work; typically single PI; 1-2 year timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this tier for pilot or exploratory studies; scope, budget, and timeline should match the smaller, shorter-term nature of these grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Research Grants eligibility/fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Research Grants (up to $500K) are for substantive research projects, typically multi-year (3-5 years), and may be submitted by a single PI or a team; there are three funding cycles per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design larger-scale, multi-year studies for this tier; demonstrate appropriate staffing, timeline, and budget for substantive work and for meeting the expectations of a larger award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision Grants are large strategic grants intended for transformative work in education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target these only for ambitious, potentially transformative projects; proposals should clearly argue for transformative potential and scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Racial Equity Research Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Racial Equity Research Grants are specifically for racial equity research in education and are issued as a distinct call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must address racial equity in education and follow any distinct call guidelines; demonstrate subject-matter fit and relevance to equity goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyle Spencer Research Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Lyle Spencer Research Awards are for distinguished mid-career scholars and can be up to $1 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for established mid-career researchers proposing work of outstanding promise; proposals should reflect the scale and prestige of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Process requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The application process typically requires a Letter of Intent (LOI); selected applicants are invited to submit a full proposal, which undergoes external peer review and then Spencer Foundation board approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare an LOI that clearly communicates significance and fit; be ready for external peer review and board decision timelines. Follow submission instructions and deadlines for chosen funding cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on intellectual ambition over incremental work
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation places a strong emphasis on intellectual ambition over incremental work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the project to show substantive advancement in understanding rather than small, incremental contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcomes diverse methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation welcomes diverse methodologies (qualitative, quantitative, mixed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the methodology that best answers the research question and justify its appropriateness; interdisciplinary or mixed-method designs are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of education broadly construed
rubrics_metrics.description: The field of education is broadly construed by the Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects addressing a wide range of educational topics and contexts are appropriate; explicitly connect topics to education when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritizes research that bridges scholarship and practice/policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation prioritizes research that bridges scholarship and practice/policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate how the research will inform practice, policy, or public discourse and include plans for engaging stakeholders or translating findings.
